STUDYQURAN:16:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r1.claim: The idea that every human community received a messenger also appears in the cited verses.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r1.anchor: Regarding the idea that every community of human beings has been sent a messenger, see also 10:47: For every community there is a messenger

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r2.claim: Elsewhere the Qur’an says every community will have a witness and will be called to its book.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r2.anchor: Elsewhere in the Quran it is said that for every community there will be a witness (4:41; 16:84; 28:75) and that every community is called to its book (45:28).

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r3.claim: Worship of God is the heart of every revealed message, taught directly by several prophets and summarized at 21:25.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r3.anchor: The command to worship God is understood to be the heart of every revealed message and is uttered directly by several prophets, including Jesus (5:72, 117); Noah

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r4.speaker: Ashʿarite theologians
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r4.claim: Ashʿarites read the passage to mean that after revelation God guides some to belief and causes others to disbelieve.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r4.anchor: Ashʿarite theologians suggest that among them were those whom God guided; and among them were those who were deserving of error (see also 7:30c) means that, after revealing the message to all, God guides some

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r5.speaker: Muʿtazilite commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r5.claim: Muʿtazilites take deserving of error to show that misguidance is earned through moral choice, not compelled by God.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r5.anchor: Muʿtazilite commentators, however, adduce the phrase deserving of error

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r6.claim: The Qur’an elsewhere says God leads wrongdoers astray, including those who mislead others.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r6.anchor: For example, the Quran indicates that God leads astray wrongdoers in particular (14:27; R) or those who have led others astray (see v. 37).

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r7.claim: The journey command urges people to learn the fate of earlier deniers; it particularly addresses Arabs who reportedly passed destroyed peoples’ ruins while traveling, but applies more widely.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r7.anchor: The recommendation that one should journey upon the earth in order to learn the fate of earlier disbelieving people refers in particular to the Arabs, who reportedly would pass by the ruins of destroyed peoples

STUDYQURAN:16:36/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r8.claim: The spiritual value of journeying in general is discussed at 30:9.
STUDYQURAN:16:36/r8.anchor: Regarding the spiritual value of journeying in general, see 30:9c.

TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r1.claim: God sent a messenger to every past nation, as He did to the present audience, commanding worship of God alone, exclusive obedience, and sincere devotion.
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r1.anchor: فيكم بأن اعبدوا الله وحده لا شريك له

TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r2.claim: The ṭāghūt to avoid refers here to Satan, whose misguidance and diversion from God's path people must fear.
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r2.anchor: يقول: وابعدوا من الشيطان، واحذروا أن يغويكم ويصدكم عن سبيل الله

TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r3.claim: Some nations were guided to believe the messengers and obey God, so they prospered and escaped punishment; others disbelieved, denied messengers, followed ṭāghūt, and God destroyed them.
TAB-FULL:v14p216#3/r3.anchor: فممن بعثنا فيهم رسلنا من هدى الله

TABATABAI:16:35-36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r2.claim: Raghib defines taghut as any transgressor or anything worshipped besides God; the word can be singular or plural, and al-Tabatabai traces it to unjust excess.
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r2.anchor: قال الراغب الطاغوت عبارة عن كل متعد

TABATABAI:16:35-36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r3.claim: Sending a messenger to every community is a universal divine practice responding to humanity's need, as the previous verse also indicates.
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى أن بعث الرسول أمر لا يختص به أمة دون أمة بل هو سنة إلهية جارية في جميع الناس

TABATABAI:16:35-36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r4.claim: This phrase explains the mission: a messenger calls people to worship God and shun idols; a human command invites rather than compels them.
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r4.anchor: بيان لبعث الرسول على ما يعطيه السياق أي ما كانت حقيقة بعث الرسول إلا أن يدعوهم إلى عبادة الله واجتناب الطاغوت

TABATABAI:16:35-36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r5.claim: Al-Tabatabai rejects supplying an omitted ليقول لهم before the command to worship and shun taghut.
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r5.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن قول بعضهم إن التقدير ليقول لهم

TABATABAI:16:35-36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r6.claim: Every community split into two groups: some God guided to the messenger's call to worship Him and shun taghut, while error became binding for others.
TABATABAI:16:35-36/r6.anchor: أي كانت كل من هذه الأمم مثل هذه الأمة منقسمة إلى طائفتين فبعضهم هو من هداه الله

TABRISI:16:36-37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r1.claim: God sent a messenger to every community and generation, just as Muhammad was sent to his own community.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r1.anchor: كما بعثناك يا محمد رسولا إلى أمتك

TABRISI:16:36-37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r2.claim: The particle أن explains the message: worship God and shun worship of the taghut, meaning Satan and anyone who calls people to error.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r2.anchor: وأن هذه هي المفسرة ويعني بالطاغوت الشيطان

TABRISI:16:36-37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r3.claim: God guided some by granting the favor He knew would lead them to believe; they believed, so that favor is called guidance.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r3.anchor: بأن لطف له بما علم أنه يؤمن عنده فآمن فسمى ذلك اللطف هداية

TABRISI:16:36-37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r4.claim: Tabrisi also allows that the phrase means God guided them to Paradise through their faith.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد منهم فمنهم من هداه الله إلى الجنة بإيمانه

TABRISI:16:36-37/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r5.claim: He rejects guidance here as merely presenting proofs, since God made proofs equally available to believers and unbelievers.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r5.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يريد بالهداية هنا نصب الأدلة

TABRISI:16:36-37/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r6.claim: The Thamud verse is cited to contrast guidance as showing proofs with the guidance meant here.

TABRISI:16:36-37/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r7.claim: Some turned away from the messenger's call, so God forsook them; error became fixed and they would never believe.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r7.anchor: ومنهم من أعرض عما دعاه إليه الرسول فخذله الله فثبتت عليه الضلالة

TABRISI:16:36-37/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:36-37/r8.claim: An alternative gloss takes the fixed misguidance to mean the punishment and destruction that became due.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r8.anchor: وقيل معناه وجبت عليه الضلالة وهي العذاب والهلاك

TABRISI:16:36-37/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r9.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:16:36-37/r9.claim: Hasan explains the phrase as the punishment for misguidance becoming due to them.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r9.anchor: ومنهم من حقت عليه عقوبة الضلالة عن الحسن

TABRISI:16:36-37/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:36-37/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:36-37/r10.claim: People are told to travel through the lands of those punished for disbelief and see their fate, lest they follow the same path and suffer likewise.
TABRISI:16:36-37/r10.anchor: أرض المكذبين الذين عاقبهم الله إن لم تصدقوني

THALABI:v6p15#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p15#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p15#2/r3.claim: Every community received a messenger to call it to worship God and avoid ṭāghūt, meaning anything worshiped besides God.
THALABI:v6p15#2/r3.anchor: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله يعني بأن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت

THALABI:v6p15#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p15#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p15#2/r4.claim: God guides some in their religion, while error becomes binding on others who die in disbelief.
THALABI:v6p15#2/r4.anchor: فمنهم من هدى الله في دينه ومنهم من حقت أي وجبت عليه الضلالة

THALABI:v6p15#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p15#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p15#2/r5.claim: Travel and see how the lands of the deniers were destroyed by torment and ruin.
THALABI:v6p15#2/r5.anchor: فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين أي خراب منازلهم وديارهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r1.claim: The mission to every community is analogous to the Prophet’s mission to the people addressed here.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r2.claim: The command is construed as “with the worship of God,” with the preposition bi omitted before the clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r2.anchor: أي: بعبادة الله تعالى، والتقدير: بأن اعبدوا الله، فحذف الجار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r3.claim: Ṭāghūt means Satan and anyone who calls people toward error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r3.anchor: أي: الشيطان وكل من يدعو إلى الضلالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r4.claim: God guided some of them, meaning that He directed them rightly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r4.anchor: فمنهم من هدى الله}: أرشده، {ومنهم من حقت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says misguidance had become binding for them in God’s prior knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في سابق علمي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God sent messengers to command worship while retaining control over guidance and misguidance; if the polytheists sincerely believed “Had God willed, we would not have worshipped,” that claim would be true.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أعلم الله أنه بعث الرسل بالأمر بالعبادة، وهو من وراء الإضلال والهداية، وهذا يدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r7.claim: “Misguidance became binding” means unbelief became obligatory for them, as in the statements that a group was rightly guided while misguidance fell due on another and that those against whom God’s word holds will not believe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r7.anchor: ومعنى {حقت عليه الضلالة}: وجب عليهم الكفر، كما قال: {فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة} [الأعراف: 30]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r8.claim: People are told to travel and reflect on traces left by denied nations, recognizing that the same punishment may befall them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r8.anchor: ثم قال: {فسيروا} الآية، أي: فسيروا معتبرين في الأرض بآثار الأمم المكذبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r9.claim: The passage concludes by reaffirming that those upon whom misguidance has become binding will not be guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p55/r9.anchor: ثم أكد أن من حقت عليه الضلالة لا يهتدي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r1.claim: God sent a messenger to every community just as He sent Muhammad to these people.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r2.claim: The messengers called people to worship God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r2.anchor: بأن اعبدوا الله { واجتنبوا الطاغوت } الشيطان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r3.claim: Taghut means Satan and everyone who calls people to error.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r3.anchor: الشيطان وكل من يدعو إلى الضلالة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r4.claim: Some were guided by God, meaning that He guided them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r5.claim: Others were destined for error: disbelief by a prior decree.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r5.anchor: وجبت { عليه الضلالة } الكفر بالقضاء السابق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:36-37/r6.claim: Travel to reflect on the traces left by nations who rejected the messengers.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r1.claim: He reads the messengers sent to each community in the surrounding context as those destroyed by punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا} [النحل: 36] ، يعني: من أهلك بالعذاب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r2.claim: The messengers called their communities to worship God and avoid false objects of worship.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r3.claim: He identifies al-ṭāghūt as Satan, who called people to worship idols, citing 4:117.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r3.anchor: والطاغوت: الشيطان، هو دعاهم إلى عبادة الأوثان، مثل قوله: {وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī instead explains al-ṭāghūt as the idols themselves.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: {واجتنبوا الطاغوت} [النحل: 36] ، يعني: واجتنبوا الأوثان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r5.claim: The guided and those upon whom error became due are like the wretched and fortunate, as in 11:105.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r5.anchor: فمنهم من هدى الله ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r6.claim: Qatāda says the deniers were destroyed and then brought to the Fire.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p63#2/r6.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: كان عاقبتهم أن دمر الله عليهم، ثم صيرهم إلى النار.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r1.claim: Ummah broadly means a large human community gathered by common ancestry, inherited traits, shared interests or ideals, or factors such as religion, time, or homeland; its plural is umam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r1.anchor: Genel anlamıyla ümmet, çoğu aynı kökten gelen, önceki kuşaklardan devralınan özelliklerin yahut ortak menfaat ve ideallerin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r2.claim: In religious usage, ummah can mean a community following a prophet or a people belonging to a revealed religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r2.anchor: Dinî anlamda, bir peygambere inanıp onun yolundan giden cemaate, ilâhî dinlere mensup kavimler topluluğuna ümmet denir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r3.claim: The word ummah in this verse is used in its broad sense of a large human community.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r3.anchor: Konumuz olan âyette ilk anlamda kullanıldığı anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r4.claim: God sent a messenger to every people to call them to worship Him and avoid false gods; this is the central purpose of prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r4.anchor: Allah her millete, geniş insan topluluğuna bir elçi göndermiştir; bunun da gayesi sadece âyetteki öz ifadesiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r5.claim: The commentary renders taghut as “false gods.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r5.anchor: “sahte tanrılar” diye çevirdiğimiz tâgut hakkında bilgi için bk. Mâide 5/60

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r6.claim: The essence of religion and the chief purpose of sending prophets is monotheism; worship requires avoiding beliefs, ideas, and acts that undermine God's oneness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r6.anchor: dinin özü ve peygamberler gönderilmesinin ana gayesi tevhiddir; kulluğun özü de Allah’ın birliği ilkesini zedeleyecek her türlü inanç, düşünce ve davranıştan titizlikle kaçınmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r7.claim: Some peoples received guidance because they approached the truths conveyed by their prophets with good faith and open minds; others remained astray through denial, stubbornness, and refusal to compromise, like some Meccan idolaters.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:36/r7.anchor: kimi, peygamberlerinin kendilerine duyurduğu ilâhî hakikatler karşısında iyi niyetli ve ön yargısız tutumları sayesinde Allah’ın hidayetine mazhar olmuş; kimi de

BURHAN:v3p368/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p368/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p368/r4.claim: Compared with the phrase about a group on whom misguidance was decreed, the greater separation between verb and subject in the other wording better licenses omission of feminine agreement.
BURHAN:v3p368/r4.anchor: أما اللفظي فهو أن الفصل بين الفعل والفاعل في قوله

BURHAN:v3p368/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p368/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p368/r5.claim: In this verse, min refers back to the feminine noun community, so feminine agreement in haqqat is fitting; the next phrase has the same meaning, but the feminine marker echoes the referent.
BURHAN:v3p368/r5.anchor: وأما المعنوى فهو أن من في قوله

SULAMI:v1p365#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p365#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p365#2/r1.claim: God sent prophets to proclaim divine oneness, teach servanthood, and turn people away from natural impulses, desires, and passions.
SULAMI:v1p365#2/r1.anchor: قال : محمد بن الفضل : بعث الله تعالى الأنبياء عليهم السلام بإظهار الوحدانية وتعليم العبودية .

SULAMI:v1p365#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p365#2/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p365#2/r2.claim: Worship adorns the knowers; their finest state is servanthood, preferring what they owe God over what they might claim for themselves.
SULAMI:v1p365#2/r2.anchor: قال سهل : العبادة زينة العارفين وأحسن ما يكون العارف إذا كان في ميادين العبودية

ITQAN:v2p554#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p554#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p554#2/r1.claim: With a truly feminine subject, the feminine marker is usually retained; omission is possible when another word intervenes, and becomes more apt as the separation grows.
ITQAN:v2p554#2/r1.anchor: الحقيقي لا تحذف تاء التأنيث من فعله غالبا إلا إن وقع فصل

ITQAN:v2p554#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p554#2/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p554#2/r8.claim: The forms differ both because the second has more separating words, favoring omission, and because min refers to the feminine collective umma while fariq is masculine; Arabic may relax agreement when an equivalent expression lacks the marker.
ITQAN:v2p554#2/r8.anchor: لوجهين لفظي وهو كثرة حروف الفاصل في الثاني والحذف مع كثرة الحواجز أكثر ومعنوي

TUSTARI:16:36/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:16:36/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:16:36/r1.claim: Worship is the gnostics' adornment; they are at their best in service and servanthood, giving up what is theirs for what is due.
TUSTARI:16:36/r1.anchor: العبادة زينة العارفين، وأحسن ما يكون العارف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r1.claim: Ṭāghūt derives from ṭughyān, exceeding bounds; it can denote a disbeliever, sorcerer, idol, Satan, or any rebellious jinn or human.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r1.anchor: الطاغوت : اسم مأخوذ من الطغيان ، والطغيان : مجاوزة الحد . وقد سمي الكافر طاغوتا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says every object worshipped, whether stone, image, or Satan, is both jibt and ṭāghūt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : كل معبود من حجر أو صورة أو شيطان ، فهو جبت وطاغوت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj transmits the same definition from Arabic speakers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك حكى الزجاج عن أهل اللغة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r4.claim: One Quranic sense is idols, as in commands to avoid them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الطاغوت في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r7.claim: Ṭaʿām names food; ṭaʿimtu means I tasted, and istaṭʿama al-ḥadīth means asking someone to narrate.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r7.anchor: الطعام : اسم للمأكول . يقال : طعمت الشيء طعما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r8.claim: A report says that if the imam asks for prompting, the congregation should prompt him by supplying the needed recitation.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r10.claim: The Prophet describes Zamzam as food that satisfies and as a cure for illness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r10.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في زمزم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r11.claim: Ṭāʿim may describe someone in good condition with food; miṭʿām is a frequent host or a heavy eater, and muṭʿam can mean someone provided for. Ṭuʿma is food or livelihood.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r11.anchor: ويقال : رجل طاعم ، أي : حسن الحال في المطعم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r12.claim: A bow is called muṭʿima because it provides its owner with game; Dhu al-Rumma’s line supplies the poetic usage.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p410#2/r12.anchor: لأنها تطعم صاحبها الصيد ، قال ذو الرمة

SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r1.claim: أن can be explanatory because sending a messenger entails a statement, or infinitival: 'We sent him with the command to worship God.'
SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أن اعبدوا الله }: يجوز في " أن " أن تكون تفسيرية؛ لأن البعث يتضمن قولا، وأن تكون مصدرية، أي: بعثناه بأن اعبدوا.

SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r2.claim: من in both clauses may be a relative pronoun or an indefinite noun qualified by a clause; on either parse, the antecedent is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:16:36/r2.anchor: قوله: { من هدى } و { من حقت } يجوز أن تكون موصولة، وأن تكون نكرة موصوفة، والعائد على كلا التقديرين محذوف

ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r1.claim: God sent messengers to every community with the command to worship Him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r1.anchor: فأعلم الله أنه بعث الرسل بالأمر بالعبادة

ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r2.claim: God stands behind both guidance and misguidance; the verse indicates that those who said so would be truthful if they held the claim as a belief.
ZAJJAJ:v3p197#2/r2.anchor: فهذا يدل على أنهم لو قالوا ذلك معتقدين لكانوا صادقين

ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r1.claim: Asad notes that ummah may mean a period of time, yielding the alternative rendering “at every period.”
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r1.anchor: Or "at every period", since the term ummah has this significance as well.

ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r2.claim: In a wider sense, Asad allows ummah to mean a civilization, encompassing both a human group and a period of time.
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n33/r2.anchor: In its wider sense, it may also be taken here to denote "civilization", thus comprising a human groupment as well as a period of time.

ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n34/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n34/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n34/r1.claim: Qur'anic worship of God entails human responsibility; this concise command sums up ethical duties and prohibitions, grounds all morality, and conveys the unchanging message of every true religion.
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n34/r1.anchor: the above commandment comprises, in the most concise formulation imaginable, the sum-total of all ethical injunctions and prohibitions

ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n35/r1.claim: Those whom God guided are the people who availed themselves of guidance He offered to all human beings.
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n35/r1.anchor: who availed themselves of the guidance offered by Him to all human beings.

ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase literally as error having inevitably become established against someone, or a verdict of error becoming inevitable for them.
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r1.anchor: upon whom error came to be inevitably established (haqqa 'alayhi)

ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r2.claim: The person in question is one whose heart God seals because of persistent, conscious refusal to submit to His guidance.
ASAD-NOTES:16:36#n36/r2.anchor: one whose heart "God has sealed" in consequence of his persistent, conscious refusal to submit to His guidance

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10#3/r2.claim: The following declaration that every community was called to worship God and avoid idols reinforces why worship language suits al-Nahl's context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10#3/r2.anchor: ومما حسّن ذلك أيضاً قوله تعالى: {وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَّسُولاً أَنِ اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت}

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r3.claim: With feminine agreement, the context is worldly life and الضلالة means misguidance itself, so the verb agrees with the feminine noun.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r3.anchor: وعندما تكون الضلالة بالتأنيث يكون الكلام في الدنيا فلمّا كانت الضلالة بمعناها هي يؤنّث الفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r1.claim: A feminine noun may take masculine agreement when the intended sense is masculine, a construction called agreement by meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r1.anchor: فإذا قصدنا باللفظ المؤنّث معنى المذكّر جاز تذكيره وهو ما يُعرف بالحمل على المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.claim: When الضلالة takes masculine agreement, the author reads it as punishment in the afterlife, where actual misguidance is absent because realities become clear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.anchor: في كل مرة يذكر فيها الضلالة بالتذكير تكون الضلالة بمعنى العذاب لأن الكلام في الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r3.claim: Feminine agreement with الضلالة occurs in worldly contexts, where the word means misguidance itself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r3.anchor: وعندما تكون الضلالة بالتأنيث يكون الكلام في الدنيا فلمّا كانت الضلالة بمعناها هي يؤنّث الفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r2.claim: Masculine agreement is licensed when the feminine word is meant in a masculine sense, by agreement with meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r2.anchor: فإذا قصدنا باللفظ المؤنّث معنى المذكّر جاز تذكيره وهو ما يُعرف بالحمل على المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.claim: Masculine agreement with الضلالة signals punishment in the afterlife; feminine agreement signals worldly misguidance, since realities are disclosed in the hereafter.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.anchor: في كل مرة يذكر فيها (الضلالة) بالتذكير تكون (الضلالة) بمعنى العذاب لأن الكلام في الآخرة

QIRAAT-ER:16:36:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:36:9#1/r1.speaker: vhr
QIRAAT-ER:16:36:9#1/r1.claim: Kasra on nūn is explained by two adjacent quiescent letters; ḍamma follows the preceding nāʾ or the vowel in ʿibāda.
QIRAAT-ER:16:36:9#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: kasra on nūn (an-i) → ḍamma (an-u); both canonical among the Seven. The kasra is due to the meeting of two sākinas

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the verse as evidence against God's willing evil: each community received a messenger commanding faith and worship of God and forbidding false gods; guidance or abandonment reflects fitness for divine favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ولقد أمد إبطال قدر السوء ومشية الشر بأنه ما من أمة إلا وقد بعث فيهم رسولا يأمرهم بالخير الذي هو الإيمان وعبادة الله واجتناب الشر الذي هو الطاغوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r2.claim: On al-Zamakhshari's account, God guides those fit for لطف and forsakes those fixed in unbelief who will yield no good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r2.anchor: فمنهم من هدى الله أي لطف به، لأنه عرفه من أهل اللطف، ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة أي ثبت عليه الخذلان والشرك من اللطف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says to observe the fate of deniers to remove doubt that God creates or wills evil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r3.anchor: فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا ما فعلت بالمكذبين حتى لا تبقى لكم شبهة وإني لا أقدر الشر ولا أشاؤه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r4.claim: Following “the messengers have only to convey clearly,” this explains their mission: worship God and avoid worshipping anything else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r4.anchor: ولما قال: فهل على الرسل إلا البلاغ المبين، بين ذلك هنا بأنه بعث الرسل بعبادته وتجنب عبادة غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r5.claim: Some respond and God guides them; others turn away and disbelieve, as confirmed by inspecting the fate of earlier deniers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p528/r5.anchor: فمنهم من اعتبر فهداه الله، ومنهم من أعرض وكفر، ثم أحالهم في معرفة ذلك على السير في الأرض واستقراء الأمم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p530/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p530/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p530/r8.claim: An alternative connects ليبين to the sending of a messenger in every nation, who exposes their disagreement and former error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p530/r8.anchor: وقيل: تتعلق ليبين بقوله: ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا، أي: ليظهر لهم اختلافهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r1.claim: God sent a messenger to every former nation commanding worship of Him alone and avoidance of every call to misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r1.anchor: من الأمم الخالية ( رسولا أن اعبدوا الله ( وحده واجتنبوا الطاغوت

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r2.claim: Al-Ṭāghūt is anything that calls people toward misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r2.anchor: الطاغوت هو كل ما يدعو إلى الضلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies al-ṭāghūt as Satan; avoiding him means avoiding what he calls people to do.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن : هو الشيطان والمراد من اجتابه اجتناب ما يدعو إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r4.claim: God guided some nations to true worship and avoidance of al-ṭāghūt by granting them success.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r4.anchor: إلى الحق من عبادته أو اجتناب الطاغوت بأن وفقهم لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r5.claim: Misguidance became fixed for others because God did not grant them success or will their guidance; its pairing with divinely willed guidance implies that it too occurs by divine will.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r5.anchor: ثبتت ووجبت إذ لم يوفقهم ولم يرد هدايتهم ووجه الإشارة أن تحقق الضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects that willing evil is itself evil: evil characterizes its acquirer, not God’s willing or creating it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r6.anchor: لأن القبيح كسب القبيح والاتصاف به لا إرادته وخلقه على ما تقرر في الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī says both interpretive hints are obscure and questions why the division must be exclusive, especially if the next clause points to aspects of the first objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r7.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن كلتا الإشارتين في غاية الخفاء ولينظر أي حاجة إلى الحصر وما المراد به

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r8.claim: The Imam reads the polytheists’ objection as: if everything is from God, sending prophets is futile; he replies that this wrongly demands reasons for God’s acts, since God rules as He wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r8.anchor: وقال الإمام : إن المشركين أرادوا من قولهم ذلك أنه لما كان الكل من الله تعالى كان بعثه الأنبياء عليهم السلام عبثا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r9.claim: The Imam says one cannot ask God why He acted or refrained from acting in a particular way.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137/r9.anchor: إذ لله سبحانه أن يفعل في ملكه ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد ولا يجوز أن يقال له لم فعلت هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p137#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137#2/r1.claim: The verse shows God’s practice of sending every community messengers to command worship of Him alone; some accept guidance and others incur error.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p137#2/r1.anchor: والدليل على أن الإنكار إنما توجه إلى هذا المعنى أنه تعالى صرح بهذا المعنى في قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r8.claim: The verse may allude to divine willing according to each person’s inward preparedness, though al-Ālūsī cautions that this reading is somewhat remote and disputable.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r8.anchor: وفي قوله سبحانه : ( ولقد بعثنا ) الخ إشارة يتفطن لها من له قلب إلى أن المشيئة حسب الاستعداد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r9.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the verse presents a divine practice among all nations: messengers guide those God wills to guide and increase the misguidance of those He wills to misguide, like food affecting sound and diseased constitutions differently.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p138/r9.anchor: والذي ذكره القاضي في قوله تعالى : ( ولقد بعثنا ) الخ أنه بين فيه أن البعثة أمر جرت به السنة الإلهية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r1.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r1.claim: The verse explains how divine will relates to voluntary acts: after the command to worship and avoid false gods, some choose guidance and others persist in error through obstinacy.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r1.anchor: وفي إرشاد العقل السليم أنه تحقيق لكيفية تعلق مشيئته تعالى بأفعال العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r2.claim: The fāʾ in فمنهم is an explanatory or resumptive fāʾ that signals an omitted consequence of the preceding statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r2.anchor: والفاء في ( فمنهم ) فصيحة كما أشير إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r3.claim: The expected parallel was ومنهم من أضل الله; the chosen wording emphasizes that error results from their bad choice, as in God’s healing attribution in 26:80.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r3.anchor: وكان الظاهر في القسم الثاني ومنهم من أضل الله إلا أنه غير الأسلوب إلى ما في النظم الكريم للإشعار

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r4.claim: In أن اعبدوا, an may be explanatory after the command sense of بعثنا, or a verbal noun with an understood preposition: بأن اعبدوا.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r4.anchor: لما في البعث من معنى القول وأن تكون مصدرية بتقدير حرف الجر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r5.claim: The address to travel is directed at the polytheist deniers who claimed that God would not have allowed their worship if He had willed otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r5.anchor: أيها المشركون المكذبون القائلون : لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r6.claim: The ruins of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those like them provide examples of the fate of deniers whose error was confirmed.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r6.anchor: من عاد وثمود ومن سار سيرهم ممن حقت عليه الضلالة وقال كما قلتم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r7.claim: The command to travel follows notice of their misguidance without first announcing punishment, since the outcome needs no further explanation; the second fāʾ urges prompt reflection that can rescue from error.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p139/r7.anchor: وترتيب الأمر بالسير على مجرد الأخبار بثبوت الضلالة عليهم من غير إخبار بحلول العذاب للإيذان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r6.claim: As God sent messengers to earlier communities, He sent one to this community too.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r6.anchor: {ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا} أي: كما بعثنا فيكم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r7.claim: The command is to worship God and avoid every object worshipped besides Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r7.anchor: {أن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت} وهو كل معبود من دون الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r8.claim: Some were guided by God to His religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r8.anchor: {فمنهم من هدى الله} أي: هداه الله إلى دينه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r9.claim: Others were subject to misguidance by prior decree and died in disbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r9.anchor: {ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة} أي: وجبت بالقضاء السابق حتى مات على كفره،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r10.claim: Travel and see that the deniers' fate was the ruin of their homes through punishment and destruction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p18/r10.anchor: {فسيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين} أي: مآل أمرهم، وهو خراب منازلهم بالعذاب والهلاك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r3.claim: What God wills occurs through appointed means; sending messengers to every nation is a divine practice that guides seekers and increases the misguidance of those destined for it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r3.anchor: وما شاء الله وقوعه إنما يجب وقوعه لا مطلقا بل بأسباب قدرها له

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r4.claim: Every messenger called people to worship God and shun the false deity or tyrant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r4.anchor: يأمر بعبادة الله تعالى واجتناب الطاغوت

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r5.claim: God guided some by enabling them to believe; others remained astray because He did not grant or will guidance, affirming that settled misguidance is by God's act and will.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r5.anchor: ومنهم من حقت عليه الضللة } إذ لم يوفقهم ولم يرد هداهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r6.claim: The address tells Quraysh to travel and consider the fate of Aad, Thamud, and other deniers as a lesson.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:33-36/r6.anchor: { فسيروا فى الأرض } يا معشر قريش

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r1.claim: Because the preceding plural “messengers” implies distribution among communities, this verse makes that distribution explicit, answers the expected question, rebuts objections to sending messengers, consoles the Prophet, and urges reflection.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r1.anchor: ولما كان جمع الرسل مفهما لتوزيعهم على الأمم , كان موضع توقع التصريح بذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r2.claim: God sent a messenger to every earlier nation; Biqāʿī states that no one on earth was left unreached by the call.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r2.anchor: من الأمم الذين قبلكم { رسولا } فما بقي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r3.claim: The verse does not say that the messenger was “from among them,” since messengers could address people outside their own community: Lot and Shuʿayb among the people of al-Aykah, and Solomon among those beyond Israel.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r3.anchor: ولأجل أن الرسل قد تكون من غير المرسل إليهم كلوط وشعيب عليهما السلام في أصحاب الأيكة وسليمان عليه السلام في غير بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r4.claim: The messengers went to their peoples proclaiming worship of God alone and strenuous avoidance of false gods, as commanded by God’s messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r4.anchor: أي الملك الأعلى وحده { واجتنبوا } أي بكل جهدكم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r5.claim: The nations divided: God guided some to truth, who saw it and obeyed the callers and thereby merited Paradise; others had error fixed upon them and incurred punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r5.anchor: فكان من غير شك بعضهم مرض لله وبعضهم مغضب له , فإنه لا يكون حكم المتنافيين واحدا أبدا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r6.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes divine command, which may not be fulfilled, from divine will, which necessarily occurs; the misguided reject the command but act within what God wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r6.anchor: فإن الأمر قد لا يكون ما تعلق به , والإرادة لا بد أن يكون ما تعلقت به

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r7.claim: If everything willed by God were morally right, both groups would be right and neither could be punished; instead, the disobedient were punished and the obedient saved in every nation, as the messengers said.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r7.anchor: فلو كان كل ما شاءه حقا كان الفريقان محقين فلم يعذب أحدهما , لكنه لم يكن الأمر كذلك , بل عذب العاصي ونجى الطائع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r8.claim: The contrast establishes the truthfulness of the messengers and the falsehood of their opponents; those who disobeyed had no remaining excuse to defend themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p267/r8.anchor: فدل ذلك قطعا على صدق الرسل وكذب مخالفيهم , فالآية من الاحتباك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r1.claim: Biqāʿī says citing those God guided first provides evidence for the following statement that misguidance has become due for others.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r1.anchor: ذكر فعل الهداية أولا دليلا على فعل الضلال ثانيا دليلا على حقوق الهداية أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r2.claim: After the decisive proof accessible to insight, the address turns to the audience because only sensory evidence remains to persuade them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r2.anchor: ثم التفت إلى مخاطبتهم إشارة إلى أنه لم يبق بعد هذا الدليل القطعي في نظر البصيرة إلا الدليل المحسوس للبصر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r3.claim: Those doubting the messengers are told to travel through the earth and inspect the dwellings and traces of past rejecters.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r3.anchor: أي فإن كنتم أيها المخاطبون في شك من إخبار الرسل فسيروا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r4.claim: The audience should look at the dwellings and remains of those who denied the messengers after passing through their lands.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r4.anchor: إذا سرتم ومررتم بديار المكذبين وآثارهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r5.claim: The fāʾ signals immediate succession, fitting an urgent proof that should pull people from error; compare the slower ثم in 6:11.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r5.anchor: وعبر هنا بالفاء المشيرة إلى التعقب دون تراخ لأن المقام للاستدلال المنقذ من الضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r6.claim: The interrogative presents the rejecters’ fate as something people ought to ask about and learn from.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r6.anchor: وأشار بالاستفهام إلى أن أحوالهم مما يجب أن يسأل عنه للاتعاظ به

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r7.claim: The rejecters include ʿĀd and later peoples whose stories reached the audience from disbelieving ancestors whom they imitated.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r7.anchor: من عاد ومن بعدهم الذين تلقيتم أخبارهم عمن قلدتموهم في الكفرمن أسلافكم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r8.claim: They chose to disobey the messengers, although this occurred within God’s will; their chosen violation of His command made the proof stand against them by ordinary human standards.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p268/r8.anchor: فأوقعت بهم لأنهم خالفوا أمري باختيارهم مع جهلهم بإرادتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r1.claim: This elaborates the preceding rebuttal of the polytheists' excuse: the messengers-only-clear-delivery statement is detailed here, and the earlier example of predecessors is explained by guided and doomed peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { كذلك فعل الذين من قبلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r2.claim: Every people received a messenger commanding worship of God and avoidance of idols; some were guided to believe, while others persisted in error and perished, as travel reveals.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r3.claim: أن is explanatory because sending a messenger to convey a message implies speaking.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r4.claim: الطاغوت is a generic term for idols worshipped besides God; its plural form is الطواغيت.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r5.claim: Attributing guidance to God answers the excuse in 16:35: He showed the way to all, and those who followed His clarification were guided by Him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r6.claim: Saying misguidance became binding, rather than directly saying God misled them, signals that their own resolve to persist kept their earlier error fixed; misguidance is their proximate doing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r6.anchor: والتعبير في جانب الضلالة بلفظ حقت عليهم دون إسناد الإضلال إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r7.claim: Other verses also ascribe misguidance to God, including 6:125 and, on the majority reading, the verse immediately following.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r7.anchor: ولكن ورد في آيات أخرى أن الله يضل الضالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r8.claim: The two attributions fit together: human error follows accumulated proximate causes across minds, temperaments, imitation, and false preaching; ultimately God created those causes and their laws.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p149/r8.anchor: فباعتبار الأسباب المباشرة كان ضلالهم من حالات أنفسهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r1.claim: After 16:35 says messengers only have clear conveyance, this verse explains that God sent messengers commanding worship of Him and avoidance of other worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r1.anchor: لما أشار قوله تعالى: فهل على الرسل إلا البلاغ المبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r2.claim: Taghut is anything worshipped besides God, whether a consenting human, stone, or wood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r2.anchor: والطاغوت في اللغة كل ما عبد من دون الله من آدمي راض بذلك، أو حجر أو خشب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r3.claim: Some reflect and God guides them through insight; others turn away and disbelieve, with misguidance leading decisively to Hell or worldly punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r3.anchor: منهم من اعتبر وهداه الله ونظر ببصيرته، ومنهم أيضا من أعرض وكفر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r4.claim: People are directed to investigate past nations and see the outcomes of those who denied the messengers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p392#2/r4.anchor: ثم أحالهم في علم ذلك على الطلب في الأرض واستقراء الأمم والوقوف على عواقب الكافرين المكذبين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r1.claim: The messenger's command to worship God means to affirm His oneness; the mission is like the Prophet's mission to his people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r1.anchor: أي كما بعثناك في هؤلاء ( أن اعبدوا الله ) أي وحدوه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r2.claim: The ṭāghūt to be avoided is Satan.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r3.claim: God's guidance here means that He guided and directed them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r3.anchor: ( فمنهم من هدى الله ) أي أرشده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r4.claim: Misguidance was established for them in God's prior knowledge; God makes clear that messengers command worship while guidance and misguidance remain with Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r4.anchor: ( ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة ) أي وجبت في سابق علم الله فأعلم الله عز وجل أنه إنما بعث الرسل بالأمر بالعبادة وهو من وراء الإضلال والهداية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r5.claim: People are told to travel while reflecting on the traces of nations that denied their messengers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p445#3/r5.anchor: ( فسيروا في الأرض ) أي معتبرين بآثار الأمم المكذبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r3.claim: God sent a messenger in every people and era, all calling people to worship God alone and reject other worship, from Noah, the first messenger to earth’s people, to Muhammad, whose mission reached humans and jinn in east and west.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r3.anchor: وبعث في كل أمة رسولا أي: في كل قرن من الناس وطائفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r4.claim: The universal prophetic call is supported by the statements that every messenger was given the revelation that there is no god but God, and that earlier messengers were asked whether deities besides the Merciful were to be worshipped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r4.anchor: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r5.claim: God’s revealed will opposes shirk because He forbade it through His messengers; His creative will merely allowed it to occur, which gives polytheists no defense. God does not approve disbelief, though He created the Fire and its inhabitants, and His proof and wisdom are decisive.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570/r5.anchor: فمشيئته تعالى الشرعية منتفية (7) ؛ لأنه نهاهم عن ذلك على ألسنة رسله، وأما مشيئته الكونية، وهي (8) تمكينهم من ذلك قدرا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.claim: After the messengers warned people, God punished some who disobeyed in this world; people are told to travel and see the end of those who denied the truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p570#2/r1.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى قد أخبر أنه عير (10) عليهم، وأنكر (11) عليهم بالعقوبة في الدنيا بعد إنذار الرسل؛ فلهذا قال:

JISHUMI:v6p3999/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r2.claim: Tawhid is the most important matter, so every prophet begins with it and then proceeds to the revealed laws.
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن أهم الأمور التوحيد لذلك بدأ كل نبي بذلك، ثم ثنى بالشرائع.

JISHUMI:v6p4029/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r9.claim: Haqqa means to become binding or established; one can say that a judgment became due upon someone.
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r9.anchor: وحق: وجب، يقال: حققت عليه القضاء حقا، وأحققته أوجبته

JISHUMI:v6p4029/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r10.claim: The author cites the Quranic form استحقا إثما as an example of becoming liable for something.

JISHUMI:v6p4029/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r12.claim: The phrase is accusative with an implied say or they said; another analysis supplies the preposition bi, meaning that they should worship God.
JISHUMI:v6p4029/r12.anchor: أن اعبدوا الله محله نصب على تقدير: قولوا اعبدوا الله، أو قالوا، وقيل: بتزع الخافض، بتقدير: بأن اعبدوا الله

JISHUMI:v6p4033/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r1.claim: The people acknowledged God despite their associating partners with Him; recognition of God can coexist with shirk.
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r1.anchor: تدل الآية أن القوم كانوا مع شركهم مقرين بالله، وأن المعارف بالله قد تكون شركا

JISHUMI:v6p4033/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r2.speaker: المجبرة
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r2.claim: The people held a position like the Mujbira's: God wills unbelief and sins.
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن القوم كانوا متمسكين بمثل مذهب المجبرة في الإرادة وأنه تعالى يريد الكفر والمعاصي

JISHUMI:v6p4033/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r3.claim: They invoked God's willing their shirk as an excuse and argued for it; God refutes them, since the messengers taught the opposite. Their belief was sincere, not mockery.
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r3.anchor: وتدل على أنهم احتجوا به وظنوه عذرا كما ظن هؤلاء فكذبهم الله، وبين أن مقالة الرسل خلاف مقالتهم

JISHUMI:v6p4033/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r4.claim: A messenger is responsible for conveying the message and must remain alive until he has delivered it.
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن على الرسول الإبلاغ، فتدل على أنه لا بد أن يبقى حتى يؤدي

JISHUMI:v6p4033/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r5.claim: God sent a messenger to every community.
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r5.anchor: (ولقد بعثنا) أي: أنه بعث في كل أمة رسولا

JISHUMI:v6p4033/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r6.claim: The messengers taught the laws, called people to monotheism and justice, and urged reflection on proofs; they began with these foundations because the laws depend on them.
JISHUMI:v6p4033/r6.anchor: وتدل على أنهم كما بينوا الشرائع دعوا إلى التوحيد والعدل. وحثوا على النظر في الدلائل، وأنهم بدأوا به

MUQATIL:16:35-37/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r5.claim: Every community received a messenger calling people to worship and affirm God's oneness and to avoid the worship of idols.
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r5.anchor: يعني أن وحدوا الله، { واجتنبوا الطاغوت }

MUQATIL:16:35-37/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r6.claim: God guided some to His religion, while misguidance became due for others; the latter were punished in this world, as the land's remains show.
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r6.anchor: فمنهم من هدى الله } إلى دينه

MUQATIL:16:35-37/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r7.claim: The command to travel and see warns Mecca's disbelievers to avoid the punishment that befell earlier communities who denied their messengers.
MUQATIL:16:35-37/r7.anchor: رسلهم بالعذاب الذين حقت عليهم الضلالة في الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r1.claim: Every messenger called people to worship and affirm God's oneness, and avoid the taghut, meaning Satan and obedience to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله ﴾ بأن وحدوه ﴿ واجتنبوا الطاغوت ﴾ الشيطان يعنى طاعته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r2.claim: God guides those who chose guidance; misguidance becomes binding on those who chose it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r2.anchor: ﴿ فمنهم من هدى الله ﴾ لاختيارهم الهدى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r3.claim: Travel and see how God destroyed the deniers and emptied their homes.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p255#6/r3.anchor: حيث أهلكهم الله وأخلى ديارهم عنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r1.claim: Every community received a messenger calling its people to worship God alone and affirm His oneness.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r2.claim: Taghut includes every object worshipped besides God: Satan, a soothsayer, an idol, or anyone summoning people to misguidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r2.anchor: أي اتركوا كل معبود دون الله كالشيطان والكاهن والصنم

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r3.claim: God guided some people by directing them to His religion and worship.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r4.claim: For others, misguidance took effect by prior decree, and they died in unbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r4.anchor: أي بالقضاء السابق عليه حتى مات على كفره

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r5.claim: Qurṭubī uses the distinction to refute the Qadariyya, who say God guided and enabled all people to reach guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r5.anchor: وهذا يرد على القدرية لأنهم زعموا أن الله هدى الناس كلهم ووفقهم للهدى

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r6.claim: The command is to travel through the land reflectively and take warning.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r7.claim: The deniers' end was ruin, punishment, and destruction.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:36/r7.anchor: أي كيف صار آخر أمرهم إلى الخراب والعذاب والهلاك

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r1.claim: God sent a particular messenger to each nation, as He sent Muhammad to his community.

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r2.claim: The particle an explains the sending: God instructed each messenger to tell his people to worship Him alone.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r2.anchor: أن مفسرة لبعثنا أي : قلنا لهم على لسان الرسول

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r3.claim: The commanded worship is worship of God alone.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r3.anchor: على لسان الرسول اعبدوا الله وحده

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r4.claim: Taghut is Satan and everything that calls people toward error.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r4.anchor: هو الشيطان وكل ما يدعوا إلى الضلال

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r5.claim: The command to worship God and avoid taghut completes the proof and removes excuses, despite God's knowing some will disobey and disbelieve.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r5.anchor: وذلك لإلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة مع علمه أن منهم من لا يأتمر بالأوامر

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r6.claim: Taghut follows the pattern faʿalūt like jabarūt and malakūt; its source form is ṭugh-yūt, with the lām moved before the ʿayn and an extra tāʾ that is not feminine.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r6.anchor: والطاغوت فعلوت من الطغيان كالجبروت والملكوت من الجبر والملك وأصله طغيوت

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r7.claim: Minhum refers to the nations, and the fāʾ supplies an understood consequence: after the messengers delivered their charge, the people divided.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r7.anchor: أي : من تلك الأمم والفاء فصيحة

BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r8.claim: God creates guidance to the truth in those who are guided, after they direct their partial power and choice toward worship and avoiding taghut.
BURSEVI:v5p24#3/r8.anchor: خلق فيه الاهتداء إلى الحق الذي هو عبادته واجتناب الطاغوت بعد صرف قدرتهم واختيارهم الجزئي

BURSEVI:v5p25/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p25/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p25/r1.claim: Misguidance becomes fixed until death because of defiance and persistence; God does not create guidance in such a person or will to purify the person's heart.
BURSEVI:v5p25/r1.anchor: أي : وجبت وثبتت إلى حين الموت لعناده وإصراره عليها وعدم صرف قدرته

BURSEVI:v5p25/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p25/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p25/r2.claim: The command to travel and observe addresses the Quraysh; the immediate fāʾ signals that they should promptly reflect and infer, so they leave error.
BURSEVI:v5p25/r2.anchor: وفي الفاء الموضوعة للتعقيب إشارة إلى وجوب المبادرة إلى النظر والاستدلال

BURSEVI:v5p25/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p25/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p25/r3.claim: The Quraysh should take warning from the destroyed homes and traces of ʿĀd, Thamud, and others who followed their way.
BURSEVI:v5p25/r3.anchor: من عاد وثمود ومن سار بسيرتهم ممن حقت عليه الضلالة لعلكم تعتبرون

RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r1.claim: Rāzī calls this the third objection of those denying prophethood: if God wills faith or unbelief, it occurs whether or not a messenger comes, so sending messengers has no purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r1.anchor: هذا هو الشبهة الثالثة لمنكري النبوة ، وتقريرها : أنهم تمسكوا بصحة القول بالجبر على الطعن في النبوة

RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r2.claim: Rāzī says this is the same objection attributed to polytheists in 6:148, and the Muʿtazilites deploy the same argument; its discussion parallels that earlier passage.
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r2.anchor: هذه الشبهة هي عين ما حكى الله تعالى عنهم في سورة الأنعام في قوله : { سيقول الذين أشركوا لو شاء الله ما أشركنا

RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r3.claim: Rāzī’s answer is that God’s established practice is to command every community to worship Him and avoid idols, while creating faith in some people and unbelief in others.
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r3.anchor: فبين تعالى أن سنته في عبيده إرسال الرسل إليهم ، وأمرهم بعبادة الله ونهيهم عن عبادة الطاغوت

RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r4.claim: A demand that God justify His acts is invalid: He rules and acts as He wills, and no one may challenge Him by asking why He acted or refrained.
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r4.anchor: كان إيراد هذا السؤال من هؤلاء الكفار موجبا للجهل والضلال والبعد عن الله

RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r5.claim: Their blame lies not in asserting that God’s will governs worship, but in supposing that this would make sending prophets impermissible; that inference is false and merits condemnation.
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r5.anchor: لا لأنهم كذبوا في قولهم : { لو شاء الله ما عبدنا من دونه } بل لأنهم اعتقدوا أن كون الأمر كذلك يمنع من جواز بعثة الأنبياء والرسل

RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r6.speaker: المتكلمون والمفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r6.claim: Earlier theologians and exegetes say the polytheists spoke sarcastically, like Shuʿayb’s people calling him forbearing and upright; Rāzī rejects this as the answer, since sincere belief in the remark would make them believers.
RAZI-FULL:v20p23/r6.anchor: من تقدمنا من المتكلمين والمسفرين فقد ذكروا فيه وجها آخر فقالوا : إن المشركين ذكروا هذا الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r4.claim: The verse shows that God guides some to faith and truth and leaves others astray, although He has commanded all communities to believe and forbidden unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه تعالى كان أبدا في جميع الملل والأمم آمرا بالإيمان وناهيا عن الكفر

RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r5.claim: Rāzī argues that command and will can diverge: the command to believe is universal, while God wills faith only for some; the Muʿtazilites instead align command with will, though they allow knowledge and will to differ.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r5.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن أمر الله تعالى لا يوافق إرادته ، بل قد يأمر بالشيء ولا يريده وينهى عن الشيء ويريده

RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r6.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says being guided means attaining God’s reward and paradise, while established deviation means punishment, not the act of unbelief or sin.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r6.anchor: أجاب الجبائي : بأن المراد : { فمنهم من هدى الله } لنيل ثوابه وجنته : { ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة } أي العقاب

RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r7.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r7.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī appeals to the following command to travel and observe the fate of deniers: it points to punishment and annihilation of earlier peoples as the intended ‘deviation.’
RAZI-FULL:v20p24/r7.anchor: وأيضا قال تعالى بعده : { فسيروا فى الارض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة المكذبين } وهذه العاقبة هي آثار الهلاك لمن تقدم من الأمم

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r1.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r1.claim: Al-Kaʿbī reads the first phrase as those who sought guidance and were judged guided by God; established deviation means their misguidance became evident, like saying an oppressor’s injustice has become manifest.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r1.anchor: وأجاب الكعبي عنه بأنه قال : قوله : { فمنهم من هدى الله } أي من اهتدى فكان في حكم الله مهتديا ، { ومنهم من حقت عليه الضلالة } يريد : من ظهرت ضلالته

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r2.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r2.claim: Al-Kaʿbī alternatively takes the phrase to mean God decrees that wrongdoers be led astray when they stray, citing 14:27.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد : حق عليهم من الله أن يضلهم إذا ضلوا كقوله : { ويضل الله الظالمين }

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r3.claim: Rāzī says decisive rational proofs already establish that guidance and misguidance come only from God; he dismisses the preceding forced interpretations as weak.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r3.anchor: بينا في آيات كثيرة بالدلائل العقلية القاطعة أن الهدى والإضلال لا يكونان إلا من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r4.claim: If God truthfully declares deviation fixed for someone, its nonoccurrence would make His report false, which is impossible; therefore their deviation necessarily occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r4.anchor: لما أخبر عنه أنه حقت عليه الضلالة امتنع أن لا يصدر منه الضلالة ، وإلا لانقلب خبر الله الصدق كذبا

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r5.claim: Rāzī cites parallel formulations about a guided group and a group rightly sentenced, those against whom God’s word has taken effect, and those against whom the decree has taken effect.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r5.anchor: ونظائر هذه الآية كثيرة منها قوله : { فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة } ( الأعراف : 30 ) وقوله : { إن الذين حقت عليهم كلمة ربك لا يؤمنون }

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r6.claim: One interpretation of ṭāghūt is all that people worship besides God, collectively called ṭāghūt.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r6.anchor: في الطاغوت قولان : أحدهما : أن المراد به : اجتنبوا عبادة ما تعبدون من دون الله ، فسمى الكل طاغوتا

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r7.claim: A second interpretation is to avoid obeying Satan when he calls people to follow him.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r7.anchor: ولا يمتنع أن يكون المراد : اجتنبوا طاعة الشيطان في دعائه لكم

RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r8.claim: The command is to travel reflectively and learn that punishment will come upon the current deniers as it came upon earlier ones.
RAZI-FULL:v20p24#2/r8.anchor: والمعنى : سيروا في الأرض معتبرين لتعرفوا أن العذاب نازل بكم كما نزل بهم
